_why: SKILL.md capped every document audit loop at TWO gating rounds on 2026-09-06, and a grep for cap logic over scripts/ returned NOTHING — prose an orchestrator can skip, which is why gateway-consolidation reached c105 with the cap on the books. Each row restores one way the cap stops binding or starts firing on the wrong population.

mutations.name: the-cap-never-fires
mutations._mechanism: Back to prose: the loop is unbounded and a 105-cycle phase reports OK.

mutations.name: the-cap-is-off-by-one-and-fires-at-the-cap
mutations._mechanism: A cap of two must PERMIT two. Firing at the cap costs a whole legitimate round every time and is how a gate gets switched off.

mutations.name: legs-are-counted-as-rounds
mutations._mechanism: A cycle emits one stamp per leg, so counting stamps counts legs: a two-leg cycle trips a cap of two on its first round. The same defect the streak had.

mutations.name: all-documents-share-one-budget
mutations._mechanism: Plan cycles are counted against the design's cap, so a document that has had one round is stopped because a SIBLING had two.

mutations.name: an-unplaceable-stamp-is-counted-as-under-cap
mutations._mechanism: A stamp whose cycle cannot be established is silently dropped, so the count is short and the cap never trips — 'I could not read it' reading as 'under the cap'.
mutations.replace:
key = cycle_of(path)
        if key is None:
            continue
        grouped.add(key)
